                    <div class="eche-report-title-question-text-wrapper">
                        <div class="eche-officer-question"> During the mobility, your institution fosters the integration of the incoming mobile participants</div>
                        <div class="eche-report-button-js eche-report-detail-close"><i class="fa fa-plus-circle fa-3x"></i></div>
                    </div>
                </div>
                <div class="eche-officer-question-wrapper eche-report-question-wrapper-show">
                    <div class="eche-report-border"></div>
                    <div classs="eche-officer-must">
                                                <h3>Must have</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">The institution appoints responsible person(s) to deal with practical issues (e.g. social, health, and/or psychological problems)</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The institution should ensure there are named, visible persons who are responsible for the practical issues associated with integrating mobile students. This visibility should be ensured through introduction to this function during the Welcome / Orientation period and be detailed on the website so all mobile students can easily access this support, throughout their stay.&nbsp;</p><p>Non-academic mentoring and support arrangements should already be outlined in the Course Catalogue of the receiving HEI, in the section on general information for students, with relevant contact persons in the respective areas. Academic advisors should have close contact with the practical services which are available to incoming participants as they are often the first line of contact to the incoming student. Further information sessions should be arranged for all staff who work with incoming students to ensure they are adequately signposted on to the appropriate services they require.</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">It appoints responsible person(s) to deal with academic issues (course timetables, student attendance, coursework, relationship with academic staff, etc.)</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>It is important that the receiving institution appoints specific named academic advisors who are responsible for dealing with problems related to academic issues (course timetables, student attendance, coursework, relationship with academic staff, etc.) of incoming students.&nbsp; Information on mentoring for thesis writing for incoming students is particularly important and clear mentoring arrangements should be agreed upon between the student, sending and receiving institutions and organised before the mobility.</p><p>For traineeships, a mentor, different from the supervisor, should be nominated to support and encourage the mobile student while in the receiving organisation. The mentor should also provide information on the culture of the enterprise and informal codes and conducts, of the receiving organisation. The contact details of both the supervisor and the mentor should be specified in the Learning Agreement.</p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-best">
                                                <h3>Best practices</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">It organises Welcome / Orientation activities at the beginning of each semester</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>An important aspect of the support arrangement is the welcome or orientation activities. These welcome / orientation activities should provide the incoming students with the necessary information on practical and administrative arrangements, to allow incoming students to meet local and other mobile students, to introduce the learning and teaching methods of the receiving institution, academic regulations, the institutional culture, health and safety issues. These activities should address any type of concern of the incoming student, and reduce any psychological pressure they might feel during their first contacts at the receiving institution. The welcome&nbsp; / orientation activities should be designed to take into account any cultural and religious sensitivities of the incoming students (ensuring a range of activities to suit different types of students).</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">It organises activities to integrate them in the receiving institution and the local community, e.g. with the support of student organisations, Erasmus+ Student and Alumni Association etc.</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>As well as academic and practical support from the institution, incoming students need to feel fully integrated into the student community, something which is best done by their fellow students / peers. Local student association(s), such as Erasmus Student Network (ESN) and the other associations’ member of the ESAA - Erasmus+ Student and Alumni Association (<a href="http://esaa-eu.org/">http://esaa-eu.org/</a>), play an important role in supporting incoming students. Incoming students need to feel welcomed and included in the student organisations. To help this process, the student organisations need to be aware of their role in supporting this integration and have access to the right resources, information, guidance and incentives. As institutions often have many types of student organisations, cooperation between them is encouraged through meetings together, social activities and buddy programmes. A key aspect of these activities is to make sure they are for all students so incoming students are integrated with the local students and hence the culture. Student organisations include for example, ESN (Erasmus Student Network) or ESAA - Erasmus+ Student and Alumni Association (<a href="http://esaa-eu.org/">http://esaa-eu.org/</a>). ESAA runs a buddy system to encourage integration of incoming students with their peers inside the institution and share good practice with other member associations around Europe.</p>                      </div>

        <h2 class="eche-report-section-title eche-pdf-page-break">After the mobility</h2>
        <div class="eche-report-section-wrapper">

                            <div class="eche-report-officer-number-text">11</div>
                        </div>
                        <div class="eche-officer-question-icon"><img class="eche-report-question-icon" src="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/profiles/custom/eac_profile/modules/eac_eche/images/ECHE__OFFICERS_Q11.png" width="100%" height="100%" alt="Question Icon" title="Question Icon" loading="lazy">
</div>

                    <div class="eche-report-title-question-text-wrapper">
                        <div class="eche-officer-question"> At the end of the mobility, your institution has formal procedures for recognising student mobility (good practices linked to recognition at the end of the mobility, e.g. in the use of Transcripts of Records and Grade Distribution Tables)</div>
                        <div class="eche-report-button-js eche-report-detail-close"><i class="fa fa-plus-circle fa-3x"></i></div>
                    </div>
                </div>
                <div class="eche-officer-question-wrapper eche-report-question-wrapper-show">
                    <div class="eche-report-border"></div>
                    <div classs="eche-officer-must">
                                                <h3>Must have</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">Transcripts of Records are issued in a timely manner (normally 5 weeks) to both incoming and outgoing students</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>It is highly important in the recognition framework to provide Transcripts of Records in a timely manner, immediately following the mobility period. After the mobility, the receiving institution should send a Transcript of Records to the student and to the sending institution within a period stipulated in the Inter-Institutional Agreement (normally within five weeks after publication/proclamation of the student’s results at the receiving institution). It can be provided electronically or through any other means accessible to the student and the sending institution. The Transcript of Records from the receiving institution should refer to the educational components agreed upon in the Learning Agreement. Grade distribution information should be included as well, either as a web link or an annex.</p><p>Following the receipt of the Transcript of Records from the receiving institution, the sending institution should automatically transfer and recognise the student’s academic outcomes successfully completed at the receiving institution, as agreed in the Learning Agreement, without the need for the student to take any further courses or exams. The Sending Institution will provide a Transcript of Records to the student or record the results in a database or any other means accessible to the student, normally within five weeks after having received the transcript of the receiving institution. The EU official template for the Learning Agreement for studies (including the Transcript of Records) is available online: <a href="http://ec.europa.eu/education/opportunities/higher-education/quality-framework_en.htm">http://ec.europa.eu/education/opportunities/higher-education/quality-framework_en.htm</a></p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">All credits gained by students during a period of study abroad that were specified in the final version of the Learning Agreement are automatically transferred by your institution and count towards the students' final degree, without the need for the student to take any further courses or exams</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The sending institution should ensure that all the credits earned by the mobile student during the mobility period are recognised and counted towards the final degree, without the need for the student to take any further courses or exams. The period of study abroad must be clear in the student's records and documents issued to the student (Diploma Supplement or equivalent). This is a golden rule of recognition of credit mobility within the framework of inter-institutional agreements. All the credits towards the student's degree that are earned during the mobility period and which were originally agreed on in the Learning Agreement (or a revised version to it) should be recognised by the sending HEI without the need for the student to take any further courses or exams. Learning Agreements are binding for all the parties and require that, on successful completion of the mobility period, the sending HEI recognises credits earned by the student and documents these credits in the student records, so they can be identified in a transparent way.</p><p>Upon receipt of the Transcript of Records or Training Certificates, the sending HEI should:<br>a) certify the mobile student has fulfilled all requirements stipulated in the Learning Agreement;<br>b) ensure recognition of the mobility period abroad within the time-scale and according to the conditions stipulated in the institutional recognition framework.</p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-best">
                                                <h3>Best practices</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">Transcripts of Records of incoming students include a description of or a link to the national grading system</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The Transcript of Records from the receiving institution should include grade distribution information, either as a web link or an annex. The local grading scale should be clearly explained, with a statistical distribution of local grades, to provide transparency and understanding of grading practices at the host institution. Where applicable, use should be made of a Grade Distribution Table for the programme of study, according to the ECTS Users’ Guide (<a href="http://ec.europa.eu/education/ects/users-guide/index.htm">http://ec.europa.eu/education/ects/users-guide/index.htm</a>).</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">Grades of outgoing students are converted, if applicable, according to a fair and transparent methodology communicated before the mobility</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>Grades of outgoing students are converted, if applicable, according to a fair and transparent methodology communicated before the mobility. There are more details on this in the ECTS Users’ Guide.</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">In addition to recognising formal learning, the institution recognises any non-formal or informal learning acquired during the mobility according to the ECTS Users’ Guide, e.g. by awarding ECTS credits for volunteering</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>During a period of mobility, students often take advantage of other opportunities outside of their required courses. These may include specific activities which can be considered non-formal or informal learning where they have acquired new skills. This could include additional language and cultural courses, extra-curricular activities, setting up a business and volunteer work undertaken by the student in that period or upon return at the receiving institution.</p>                      </div>

                    <div class="eche-report-title-question-text-wrapper">
                        <div class="eche-officer-question"> Your institution issues a Diploma Supplement</div>
                        <div class="eche-report-button-js eche-report-detail-close"><i class="fa fa-plus-circle fa-3x"></i></div>
                    </div>
                </div>
                <div class="eche-officer-question-wrapper eche-report-question-wrapper-show">
                    <div class="eche-report-border"></div>
                    <div classs="eche-officer-must">
                                                <h3>Must have</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">To all students, automatically, free of charge and in a major European language</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>This Supplement should include a record of the period of mobility under the Erasmus+ Programme. The 48 European countries taking part in the Bologna Process have agreed that each mobile graduate in their respective country should receive the Diploma Supplement (DS) automatically, free of charge and in at least one of the major European languages in addition to the national language. The HEI should issue a Diploma Supplement (or equivalent) to accompany every degree successfully completed by a student, using - where applicable - the template developed by the European Commission, the Council of Europe and UNESCO. The HEI's policy on issuing the Diploma Supplement should be published on its website.</p><p>The template for the Diploma Supplement is available at:<br><a href="http://ec.europa.eu/education/tools/diploma-supplement_en.htm">http://ec.europa.eu/education/tools/diploma-supplement_en.htm&nbsp;</a></p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-best">
                                                <h3>Best practices</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">That includes a record of the mobility period(s) carried out by the student under the Erasmus+ programme</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The information contained in the Transcript of Records from the Receiving Institution should also be included in the Diploma Supplement produced by the Sending Institution (at least for Sending Institutions located in Programme Countries), with the exact titles of the components that the student has followed abroad. Alongside modules or units taken at the sending HEI, the Diploma Supplement should list recognised modules, units and/or training activities undertaken during the student's mobility period and indicate the location of these mobility activities.<br>In the case of double, multiple or joint degrees, the Diploma Supplement should indicate the name and status of the partner HEIs awarding the degree and explain the respective language(s) of instruction and examination. In addition, an explanation should be provided about the grading and classification scheme agreed by the awarding HEIs. The template for the Diploma Supplement is available at:<br><a href="http://ec.europa.eu/education/tools/diploma-supplement_en.htm">http://ec.europa.eu/education/tools/diploma-supplement_en.htm</a>&nbsp;</p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-case">
                                                <h3>Case studies</h3>
                                                <div><a href="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/eche/the-diploma-supplement-a-tool-to-promote-international-recognition-and-transparency-of-academic-achievement" target="_blank">The Diploma Supplement – a tool to promote international recognition and transparency of academic achievement</a></div>
                                             </div>
                    <div class="eche-report-button-js eche-report-detail-close-text"><i class="fa fa-times fa-2x"></i><span>Close</span></div>
                </div>
            </div>
                         <div class="eche-report-full-question-wrapper">
                <div class="eche-officer-question-title-wrapper">
                    <div class="eche-report-title-icons-wrapper">
                                                 <div class="eche-report-officer-number">
                            <img class="eche-report-question-icon" src="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/profiles/custom/eac_profile/modules/eac_eche/images/eche-pdf/number-corner-orange-13.png" width="100%" height="100%" alt="Question Icon" title="Question Icon" loading="lazy">

                            <div class="eche-report-officer-number-text">13</div>
                        </div>
                        <div class="eche-officer-question-icon"><img class="eche-report-question-icon" src="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/profiles/custom/eac_profile/modules/eac_eche/images/ECHE__OFFICERS_Q13.png" width="100%" height="100%" alt="Question Icon" title="Question Icon" loading="lazy">
</div>
                    </div>
                    <div class="eche-report-title-question-text-wrapper">
                        <div class="eche-officer-question"> Your institution promotes and recognises staff mobility</div>
                        <div class="eche-report-button-js eche-report-detail-close"><i class="fa fa-plus-circle fa-3x"></i></div>
                    </div>
                </div>
                <div class="eche-officer-question-wrapper eche-report-question-wrapper-show">
                    <div class="eche-report-border"></div>
                    <div classs="eche-officer-must">
                                                <h3>Must have</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">By taking it into account in the assessment of their professional development </span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>Participation in international projects should be seen as an important aspect of the professional development of the staff and of the modernisation of the HEI and should, therefore, be considered a key component in staff evaluation practices.</p><p>The HEI should link its HR strategy to the objectives set out the internationalisation strategy for staff. For all staff who undertake a period of mobility, HR should be informed and provide support to ensure the identification of the professional development needs of the individual as well as setting out agreed career objectives for their period of mobility. This can be through prepared addendums to staff contracts or through less formal mechanisms of agreed objectives. The new objectives should become part of the normal system of staff evaluation or appraisal and be used in order to recognise the achievements of the staff during the period of mobility. This means that HR staff should be trained to ensure these additional objectives are formally evidenced and recorded in staff records and lead to other rewards and recognition.&nbsp;</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">Through, for example the reduction of the teaching load, promotion or pay rises</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>It is highly important to incentivise staff to participate in mobility activities. In order to support and encourage mobility, HEIs should provide a number of incentives to ensure that when staff return to the sending institution, they have long term career benefits. HEIs should acknowledge periods of mobility as a normal part of a career path. Staff working schedules and agreed objectives (in terms of research outputs and assessments) should be adapted to meet their new requirements. Temporary replacements should be found during the mobility period, where possible, to ensure continuity during the mobility period. Upon returning to the sending institution, incentives to maintain links with other institutions or networks should be put in place through providing the time to nurture new relationships (reduction in teaching or research loads, continued related objectives set in performance appraisals). The new objectives set with HR for the period of mobility should be ones which are explicitly recognised and rewarded through promotion, awards or pay rises. Additional cultural / language skills should be recognised as a component in any evaluation / assessment of the staff. This may be achieved by making it well-known that participation is a formal part of staff evaluation procedures, and may lead to improvements in both working conditions and promotion or broader career prospects.</p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-best">
                                                <h3>Best practices</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">By encouraging them to propose improvements to the institutional strategy for internationalisation and overarching structure, as well as for structural reform</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>One important form of recognition for staff, which is equally beneficial to the HEI is to encourage their involvement in improving internationalisation and structural reform within the institution. This includes the opportunity for staff to provide feedback into the management structures of departments and the overall institution. There should be a firm commitment - perhaps in writing - from the HEI to recognise and make use of constructive feedback as well as the appropriate forums for staff to engage with senior management to discuss their experiences and propose new ideas for improvement.&nbsp;</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">By inviting them to share new learning and teaching practices developed abroad with their peers in the institution</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The experience of staff should be valued and shared as an inspiration to others, by, for example, organising meetings and publishing articles where the mobile participants share their experience and the impact of mobility on their personal and professional development. Where staff are involved in teaching at host institutions, new learning and teaching practices can be brought back and shared with other staff members through seminars or presentations. Staff can be supported through the administrative and academic services to understand the skills they have acquired and how best to use them within their own institution.</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">By encouraging them to propose cooperation projects with their receiving organisation</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>Mobile staff bring back new partners, networks and ideas which can be of significant value for the HEI. Staff should be encouraged to propose and develop new or further cooperation projects between their receiving and sending institutions. This requires time and commitment, which need to be given formally by the sending institution, including, for example, additional support to write joint proposals.&nbsp;</p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-case">
                                                <h3>Case studies</h3>
                                                <div><a href="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/eche/recognition-of-staff-mobility-supporting-individuals-development-and-institutional-aims-and-objectives" target="_blank">Recognition of staff mobility – supporting individuals’ development and institutional aims and objectives</a></div>
                                                <div><a href="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/eche/recognition-of-staff-participating-in-erasmus-staff-mobility-actions-and-international-cooperation-projects" target="_blank">Recognition of staff participating in Erasmus staff mobility actions and international cooperation projects</a></div>
                                             </div>
                    <div class="eche-report-button-js eche-report-detail-close-text"><i class="fa fa-times fa-2x"></i><span>Close</span></div>
                </div>
            </div>
                         <div class="eche-report-full-question-wrapper">
                <div class="eche-officer-question-title-wrapper">
                    <div class="eche-report-title-icons-wrapper">
                                                 <div class="eche-report-officer-number">
                            <img class="eche-report-question-icon" src="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/profiles/custom/eac_profile/modules/eac_eche/images/eche-pdf/number-corner-orange-14.png" width="100%" height="100%" alt="Question Icon" title="Question Icon" loading="lazy">

                            <div class="eche-report-officer-number-text">14</div>
                        </div>
                        <div class="eche-officer-question-icon"><img class="eche-report-question-icon" src="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/profiles/custom/eac_profile/modules/eac_eche/images/ECHE__OFFICERS_Q14.png" width="100%" height="100%" alt="Question Icon" title="Question Icon" loading="lazy">
</div>
                    </div>
                    <div class="eche-report-title-question-text-wrapper">
                        <div class="eche-officer-question"> With regards to the outcomes and experiences of Erasmus+ activities</div>
                        <div class="eche-report-button-js eche-report-detail-close"><i class="fa fa-plus-circle fa-3x"></i></div>
                    </div>
                </div>
                <div class="eche-officer-question-wrapper eche-report-question-wrapper-show">
                    <div class="eche-report-border"></div>
                    <div classs="eche-officer-must">
                                                <h3>Must have</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">The results are monitored, evaluated and disseminated as a way to improve international cooperation and mobility activities</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>Linked with the overall internationalisation strategy of the institution, monitoring and evaluation of cooperation projects and Erasmus+ mobility is essential if HEIs are to learn from their experiences. Monitoring and evaluation is more than just measuring the number and types of outputs, it needs to include capturing information on the overall outcomes and experiences of the activities at the institutional and the individual level. Systematic monitoring and evaluation should therefore include more qualitative approaches, which expressly capture the experiences in a way which helps the institution to understand the added value of its involvement in these activities. Documenting and analysing the outcomes and experiences is only the first step. To learn from the approaches taken, and the benefits gained, institutions should take time to disseminate the findings of the cooperation projects and mobility periods through, for example, meetings, workshops and publications, social media, etc. These activities will embed good practice, help the institution to iteratively improve its approach and also feed back into the on-going monitoring and evaluation.</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">The results are used systematically for the benefit of your institution, providing internationalisation at home, hence enhancing intercultural competences of non-mobile students and staff</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The outcomes and experiences of cooperation and Erasmus+ mobility have a much wider impact than just improving mobile activities. All institutions have significant numbers of non-mobile staff and students who can benefit from the international experiences of others. As part of the monitoring and evaluation processes, HEIs should consider the impact which can be specifically made on non-mobile staff and students, giving them “internationalisation at home experiences”. This includes building international competences, cultural awareness, virtual mobility opportunities, inviting international lecturers and embedding student projects with an international focus into the curricula, and providing opportunities for local students to work together with incoming mobile participants in e.g. project work, to ensure that local students benefit from the presence of mobile students at their institution. This fits with the activities of disseminating the overall outcomes and experiences of the cooperation projects and Erasmus+ mobility, though tailored to a different audience. It should take into account the professional development needs of the staff at the HEI and the perspectives of non-mobile students.&nbsp;</p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-best">
                                                <h3>Best practices</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">The results are exploited and disseminated, by providing participants with the results of cooperation projects and Erasmus+ mobility opportunities (e.g. presentations) to share funding possibilities</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The dissemination of outcomes is an integral part of mobility projects. Good practice would be to ensure that the dissemination is built into the support measure and participants in projects and mobility actions are allocated adequate time, resources and space to disseminate their experiences and exploit project results. This includes opportunities to share new knowledge and to highlight new opportunities (including funding) which have arisen from the new relationships formed. In order to do this, HEIs should provide support functions such as web platforms to collect results or opportunities to present results at the institutional or departmental level, as relevant.&nbsp;</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">After the mobility Erasmus+ participants have the opportunity to present their newly acquired competences</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The study entitled ‘Effects of mobility on the skills and employability of students and the internationalisation of higher education institutions’ showcases how mobility can contribute to the internationalisation of higher education institutions, including the impacts on teaching methods, cooperation between HEIs and perception of staff more generally. Therefore the dissemination of outcomes is an integral part of mobility projects. Good practice would be to ensure that the dissemination is built into the support measure and participants in projects and mobility actions are allocated adequate time, resources and space to disseminate their experiences and exploit project results. This includes opportunities to share new knowledge and to highlight new opportunities (including funding) which have arisen from the new relationships formed. In order to do this, HEIs should provide support functions such as web platforms to collect results or opportunities to present results at the institutional or departmental level, as relevant.&nbsp;</p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-case">
                                                <h3>Case studies</h3>
                                                <div><a href="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/eche/capitalising-on-the-outcomes-and-experiences-of-erasmus-activities" target="_blank">Capitalising on the outcomes and experiences of Erasmus+ activities</a></div>
                                                <div><a href="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/eche/the-erasmus-impact-study-effects-of-mobility-on-the-skills-and-employability-of-students-and-the-internationalisation-of-higher-education-institutions" target="_blank">The Erasmus Impact Study: Effects of mobility on the skills and employability of students and the internationalisation of higher education institutions</a></div>
                                             </div>
                    <div class="eche-report-button-js eche-report-detail-close-text"><i class="fa fa-times fa-2x"></i><span>Close</span></div>
                </div>
            </div>

</div>

Die REA Firmengruppe ist ein regional agierendes Ingenieurbüro für Erneuerbare Energien. Seit über 25 Jahren planen, projektieren und betreiben wir in Zusammenarbeit mit lokalen Partnern Solar- und Windenergieanlagen im Rheinland. Besonders wichtig ist uns dabei die Beteiligung von Bürgern an der Wertschöpfung unserer Projekte, womit wir auch die Bevölkerung direkt vor Ort für die Erneuerbaren Energien begeistern. Denn nur gemeinsam wird die Region erneuerbar. Der beständige Kontakt zu Hochschulen ist uns wichtig, um die aktuellen Entwicklungen der Erneuerbaren Energien, insbesondere der Windbranche, im Auge zu halten und im Ideenaustausch mit Studentinnen und Studenten zu bleiben.

  • Unterstützung der Flächenakquise durch

  • Anfrage und Verarbeitung von Katasterdaten

  • Ggf. Begleitung von Baustellenterminen

  • Allgemeine Bürotätigkeiten und Recherche

Our mission is to understand how liquids perform inside the systems they are designed to protect and optimise, from electric vehicle batteries and ultra-fast chargers to high-performance data centres and advanced electronics.<br>As part of a major investment programme, Castrol’s Pangbourne Technology Centre is evolving into a centre of excellence for electrification and energy technologies. The team operates world-class testing facilities including battery cell, module and pack laboratories, high-voltage charging systems, immersion cooling tanks, data centre server environments and large-scale thermal management test rigs.<br>This is a team for engineers who are naturally curious. You'll work in an environment that combines the freedom of university-style research with the pace and impact of commercial product development. One day you may be investigating battery cooling performance, the next developing new testing methodologies for data centre technologies or semiconductor cooling systems.<br>You'll join a highly collaborative group of engineers, technicians, graduates and researchers who are passionate about solving complex engineering challenges. We are looking for individuals who love understanding how things work, enjoy getting hands-on with equipment, and want to help create the next generation of high-performance technologies.</p> <h4>Key Tasks</h4> <p>As a Senior Engineer, you will lead research and development testing projects from concept through to final technical recommendations, working closely with internal stakeholders, technology experts and external partners.<br><br>Key responsibilities include:<br><br>- Leading end-to-end testing and engineering projects supporting Castrol's research and product development programmes.<br>- Designing, building, commissioning and operating advanced test rigs and experimental systems.<br>- Developing innovative testing methodologies for emerging technologies across electric vehicles, batteries, charging infrastructure and data centres.<br>- Designing experiments using statistical Design of Experiments (DoE) techniques and ensuring data quality and repeatability.<br>- Performing advanced data analysis and translating results into meaningful engineering insights and recommendations.<br>- Working hands-on with high-voltage systems, instrumentation, thermal management equipment and power electronics.<br>- Supporting the installation, operation and continuous improvement of testing facilities and equipment.<br>- Acting as a subject matter expert in one or more areas such as battery systems, thermal management, data centres, cooling technologies, power electronics or DC power systems.<br>- Collaborating with OEMs, technology partners and internal stakeholders to deliver co-engineered solutions.<br>- Coaching and mentoring engineers, technicians, graduates and interns while acting as a technical role model within the team.<br>- Identifying new technologies, testing opportunities and research directions that strengthen Castrol's innovation capability.<br>- Representing Castrol externally through technical engagement with customers, industry partners and research organisations.<br>- Maintaining the highest standards of safety, operational excellence and engineering integrity across all activities.</p> <h4>Experience Required</h4> <p>We're looking for an experienced, hands-on engineer with a passion for experimentation, problem-solving and developing new technologies.<br><br>You will typically bring:<br><br>- Degree-qualified in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Physics or a related engineering discipline.<br>- 5+ years' experience in a professional engineering     Ce que nous vous offrons

    • Un environnement stimulant : une dynamique startup au sein d’un groupe établi (CA de 70M€, 500 collaborateurs).

    • Des opportunités d’évolution et de formation : développez vos compétences et faites avancer votre carrière.

    Rattaché(e) au Rattaché(e) au Directeur des Opérations, vos principales missions sont les suivantes :

    • Encadre un à deux collaborateur(s) en charge du suivi quotidien de la métrologie sur l'ensemble des agences au

    niveau national.

     

    Mission principale

    Le Responsable Métrologie garantit la conformité métrologique des équipements utilisés pour le transport des échantillons biologiques. Il est responsable de l'étude, du choix, de l'installation et du suivi des matériels permettant d'assurer le maintien de la chaîne de température réglementaire dans les véhicules frigorifiques. Il travaille en étroite collaboration avec le Responsable Parc Automobile, les Responsables Exploitation et les fournisseurs afin d'assurer la fiabilité des équipements et la qualité du transport.

     

    PRINCIPALES RESPONSABILITES

    Métrologie et maîtrise de la température

    • Définir et mettre en œuvre la politique métrologique de l'entreprise.

    • Garantir le respect des exigences réglementaires relatives au transport des échantillons biologiques.

    • Assurer le suivi des équipements de mesure de température (capteurs, enregistreurs, sondes, etc.).

    • Organiser les opérations de vérification, d'étalonnage et de qualification des équipements.

    • Analyser les dérives et mettre en œuvre les actions correctives.

    • Connaître et faire appliquer les référentiels applicables : ADR (matières biologiques catégorie B – UN3373), norme NF EN 12830 (enregistreurs de température) et NF X15-140 (étalonnage) / accréditation COFRAC.

    Our Operating Principles


    Extreme Ownership

    We take full responsibility for our work, outcomes, and team success. No excuses, no blame-shifting — if something needs fixing, we own it and make it better. This means stepping up, even when it’s not “your job.” If a ball is dropped, we pick it up. If a customer is unhappy, we fix it. If a process is broken, we redesign it. We don’t wait for someone else to solve it — we lead with accountability and expect the same from those around us.

     

    Craftsmanship

    Putting care and intention into every task, striving for excellence, and taking deep ownership of the quality and outcome of your work. Craftsmanship means never settling for “just fine.” We sweat the details because details compound. We aim to deliver jaw-dropping customer experiences by being curious, meticulous, and proud of what we build — even when nobody’s watching.

    Be friendly & have fun with your coworkers. Always be genuine & honest, but kind. “Majo” is our way of saying: be a good human. Be approachable, helpful, and warm. We’re building something ambitious, and it’s easier (and more fun) when we enjoy the ride together.     Create the highest impact in the shortest amount of time. Move fast, but in the right direction. We operate with speed because time is our most limited resource. But speed without focus is chaos. We prioritize ruthlessly, act decisively, and stay aligned. We aim for high leverage: the biggest results from the simplest, smartest actions. We’re running a high-speed marathon — not a sprint with no strategy.

     

    Talent Density and Meritocracy
    Hire only people who can raise the average; ‘exceptional performance is the passing grade.’ Ability trumps seniority. We believe the best teams are built on talent density — every hire should raise the bar. We reward contribution, not titles or tenure. We give ownership to those who earn it, and we all hold each other to a high standard. A-players want to work with other A-players — that’s how we win.

     

    First-Principles Thinking
    Strip a problem to physics-level facts, ignore industry dogma, rebuild the solution from scratch. We don’t copy-paste solutions. We go back to basics, ask why things are the way they are, and rebuild from the ground up if needed. This mindset pushes us to innovate, challenge stale assumptions, and move faster than incumbents. It’s how we build what others think is impossible.

    • Co-animer le réseau des référents SAFRAN des directions régionales (DR) de l’ASP

    • Coordonner et animer le recueil des besoins métiers pour l’outil SAFRAN (instruction des aides) en lien avec l’écosystème des outils liés (gestion des enveloppes, contrôle, …) et le déploiement des dispositifs

    • Co-piloter la feuille de route de déploiement des dispositifs en lien avec la direction des opérations et co-animer les instances de pilotage associées

    • Alerter sur les difficultés (auprès de la DDRP et au donneur d’ordre), proposer des solutions

    • Animer le groupe référents dispositifs du SANF et suivre avec eux l'instrumentation, le recettage et la mise en production de SAFRAN, assurer le suivi dans des outil de gestion de projet

    Contribuer à l’animation du réseau des référents SAFRAN en D(i)R-ASP

    • Coanimer le réseau des référents SAFRAN en D(i)R – ASP en lien avec la direction des opérations (DO)

    • Copiloter avec la DO les formations des membres du réseau

    • Assurer la veille sur les évolutions de l’outil et les partager

    • Dans le domaines des dispositifs nationaux : contribuer à la préparation des réunions de secteur, contribuer à établir et à faire vivre les outils de suivi de l’activité et des projets, s'assurer du respect des échéances

    • Participer à des bilatérales avec les agents en charge des dispositifs nationaux

    • Participer aux réunions des cadres du SADRP et aux points cadres de la direction

    About Mistral

    Mistral provides full-stack AI solutions: from frontier models to developer tools, applications, and compute. We partner with enterprises tackling the hardest problems across high-stakes industries like finance, manufacturing, defense, healthcare, and the public sector, co-creating customized AI systems that they can run on their terms.

    We are a dynamic, collaborative team passionate about AI and its potential to transform society. Our diverse workforce thrives in competitive environments and is committed to driving innovation. Our teams are distributed between Europe, North America, Asia and the Middle East. We are creative, low-ego and team-spirited.

    The Role

    Evaluation is how we decide which models, checkpoints and recipes ship. As a Research Engineer on the Eval Platform team, you will build the infrastructure every science team relies on to measure model quality, and make it reliable, reproducible and fast.

    You don't need to have designed benchmarks before. You do need to care about what a score means, and about when a difference between two runs is real.

    What you will do

    • Build systems that keep eval results reproducible and comparable over time, as models, benchmarks and code evolve.

    • Run evaluations at scale across our GPU clusters, from model serving to scoring.

    • Make eval results easy to access, explore and trust, through APIs and dashboards that researchers use every day.

    • Catch broken or noisy evals before they mislead research decisions.

    • Support evaluation of agentic, multi-turn and tool-using models.

    • Work closely with researchers to turn new evaluation needs into robust, shared tooling.

    What we're looking for

    • Master's or PhD in Computer Science, or equivalent experience.

    • 4+ years building production-grade software, ideally large-scale ML codebases or distributed systems.

    • Excellent Python and strong software-design instincts: testing, code review, CI/CD.

    • Experience running workloads on GPU clusters (Slurm, Kubernetes, Ray or similar).

    • Familiarity with LLM inference and evaluation.

    • A product mindset: researchers are your users.

    • Self-starter, low-ego, collaborative.

    Nice to have

    • Experience building or maintaining evaluation harnesses or benchmarks.

    • Hands-on experience with inference engines such as vLLM or SGLang.

    • Experience with agentic or RL environments.

    • Statistics for experimentation: variance estimation, significance testing.

    • Open-source contributions to ML tooling.

    What We Offer

    We offer a comprehensive benefits package designed to support your well-being, growth, and work-life balance. Benefits vary by country and may include healthcare coverage, parental leave, retirement plans, relocation support, wellness programs, meal and transportation allowances, and other location-specific perks.

    For the most up-to-date details on benefits available in your location, please refer to our Benefits page.

    Privacy Policy

    As Destinus scales its vehicle programmes, we are looking for a dedicated Technical Project Manager to own execution across the full vehicle development stack – from propulsion and structures through avionics integration, ground support equipment, and qualification. This frees our engineers to focus on technical depth and our team leads on strategic leadership.

    As one of the first hires in this group, you will manage a programme and help build the PM structure itself alongside team leads and fellow TPMs. You own execution – schedule, cross-disciplinary coordination, risk, and delivery. The engineers run the technical depth; you run the programme.

    What You’ll Do

    · Own end-to-end execution of vehicle-level and subsystem product development programmes – from kick-off through hardware build, test campaigns, qualification, and delivery

    · Build and maintain programme plans spanning propulsion, structures, avionics, systems engineering, manufacturing, procurement, and regulatory dependencies; identify and resolve critical path risks early

    · Run programme reviews and cross-functional coordination meetings; keep decisions documented and actions closed

    · Work closely with engineering leads across disciplines to track technical progress and translate it into clear programme status

    · Coordinate system integration activities – ensuring interfaces between subsystems (propulsion, structures, avionics, GSE) are managed, dependencies tracked, and integration milestones owned

    · Manage external dependencies: supplier lead times, test facility scheduling, regulatory submissions, and customer milestones

    · Proactively flag scope creep, resource conflicts, and schedule risk to leadership – with options, not just problems

    · Contribute to building the PM structure, tools, and ways of working for the department alongside team leads and fellow TPMs

    Requirements

    Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in aerospace, mechanical, systems, or a related engineering discipline

    · 5–8 years in a hardware-heavy development environment; at least 2 in a project management, programme coordination, or technical lead role – career PMs without hardware exposure will not be considered

    · Background in aerospace, defence, or a similarly regulated hardware domain; familiarity with vehicle-level or system-level development and qualification cycles is essential

    · Experience managing cross-disciplinary programmes spanning multiple engineering domains (structures, propulsion, avionics, or similar) is a strong advantage

    · Able to manage multiple concurrent projects across engineering, manufacturing, procurement, and testing

    · Strong systems thinking – able to see the full picture, spot where the hard problems are likely to sit, and know when to dive into detail without losing the overall programme

    · Strong planning skills – able to build a programme schedule from scratch, identify critical path, and keep it current

    · Comfortable building structure in an ambiguous environment; pragmatic over bureaucratic

    · Clear, direct communicator in English; German is an advantage

About Kreato Global

Founded in 2020, Kreato Language Group LLC provides business process outsourcing and professional language services that help organizations overcome communication barriers across healthcare, legal, financial, customer service, and social service settings.

Our services include Over-the-Phone Interpretation (OPI), Video Remote Interpretation (VRI), On-Site Interpretation, and American Sign Language (ASL). We are committed to delivering accurate, reliable, and culturally sensitive communication while building a supportive environment for our remote professionals.

About the Role

We are looking for experienced English-Spanish interpreters based in Latin America to join our remote team in a blended Over-the-Phone Interpretation (OPI) and Video Remote Interpretation (VRI) role starting in October 2026.

As an interpreter, you will facilitate clear and accurate communication between English- and Spanish-speaking individuals across medical, social service, customer care, and financial settings. You will use consecutive interpretation techniques to ensure that all parties understand one another while maintaining professionalism, impartiality, confidentiality, and accuracy.

Important: A minimum of six months of verifiable professional experience in remote OPI and/or VRI interpretation is mandatory. Candidates without the required experience will not be considered.

Why Join Kreato Global?

  • Guaranteed Pay: Get paid for each eligible logged-in hour, including time spent handling calls and waiting in the queue, subject to the applicable program terms.

  • Sign-On Bonus: Earn an additional bonus in accordance with the program's eligibility requirements.

  • Performance Bonuses: Be rewarded for meeting established performance and quality standards.

  • Schedule Adherence Bonuses: Earn additional incentives for maintaining reliable attendance and schedule adherence, subject to program requirements.

  • Overtime Opportunities: Increase your earnings through available overtime shifts.

  • 100% Remote Work: Work from home with no daily commute.

  • Structured Workweek: Work five days per week, with two scheduled days off.

  • Supportive Team Environment: Join a professional team that values accuracy, reliability, collaboration, and continuous improvement.

Bonus amounts, eligibility criteria, and applicable program terms will be communicated during the recruitment process.

Key Qualifications

  • Required Experience: At least six months of verifiable professional experience providing remote English-Spanish OPI and/or VRI interpretation.

  • English Proficiency: Advanced English fluency at a minimum C1 level, with strong spoken and written communication skills.

  • Spanish Proficiency: Native or native-level Spanish fluency, with excellent comprehension and active listening skills.

  • Interpretation Skills: Ability to deliver accurate, complete, impartial, and professional consecutive interpretation.

  • Specialized Terminology: Strong knowledge of medical, financial, and social service terminology.

  • Confidentiality and Compliance: Understanding of patient privacy, confidentiality, and HIPAA-related requirements.

  • Professionalism: Excellent attention to detail, active listening, emotional composure, and the ability to remain neutral in sensitive situations.

  • Reliability: Commitment to attendance, schedule adherence, quality standards, and established operating procedures.

  • Remote Work Readiness: Ability to work independently in a quiet, professional environment with a reliable wired internet connection.

Technical Requirements

All candidates must meet the following technical requirements to be eligible for onboarding.

Internet Connection

  • A stable, reliable internet connection.

  • An Ethernet cable connected directly to the router or modem.

  • Wi-Fi is not permitted.

Approved USB Headsets

Only approved, client-compatible USB headsets are accepted. Bluetooth headsets, mono headsets, and built-in microphones are not permitted.

Approved models include:

  • Logitech H390

  • Jabra GN series / Jabra Evolve series

  • Microsoft LifeChat LX-6000

  • Plantronics Blackwire C3220

  • Dell Plantronics

  • HP Stereo USB Headset G2

The exact headset model must meet the client's technical specifications and approval requirements.

Computer and Video

  • Processor: Intel Core i5, 6th generation or newer.

  • Webcam: 720p or 1080p resolution.

  • Browser: An updated version of Chrome, Safari, Microsoft Edge, or Firefox.

  • Work Environment: A quiet, distraction-free space suitable for confidential interpretation sessions.

Start Date

October 2026

Selected candidates must be available to complete the recruitment, technical verification, and client onboarding requirements before their assigned start date.

Ready to Apply?

If you have at least six months of remote OPI/VRI interpretation experience, meet the English and Spanish proficiency requirements, and have the required technical equipment, we encourage you to apply.

Join Kreato Global and help bridge language barriers through meaningful, high-quality communication.

Apply today to be considered for our October 2026 intake!

This is a remote position.

About the Role

This is a founder’s office role. You’ll work directly with Aj (founder) on GTM execution, internal ops, and whatever else needs to get done to move the company forward.
There’s no clean job description here. Some weeks it’s building outreach systems. Some weeks it’s competitive research. Some weeks it’s figuring out why a process is broken and fixing it. The thread connecting all of it: speed, judgment, and an AI-first approach to everything.
We’re hiring for someone who’s hungry, sharp, and already deep into AI - not someone who wants to get into AI.
What You’ll Work On
• GTM support - outreach campaigns, lead research, pipeline ops, follow-up systems
• Internal ops - building and automating processes that let a small team punch above its weight
• Research & analysis - market research, competitor mapping, client/prospect context
• Content & communication- drafts, decks, summaries - whatever the founder needs turned around fast
• Ad hoc projects - if it matters to the company right now, it’s on the table

Requirements

What We’re Looking For
Non-negotiables:
• You’ve built something with AI. Not a tutorial. Not a prompt collection. An actual tool or product - even if just for yourself - using Claude, Codex, Cursor, or similar. We’ll ask you about it.
• You move fast. Not “I work hard” fast - demonstrably fast. You bias toward doing over planning.
• You learn quickly and openly. You don’t need to know everything coming in. You do need to figure things out without being hand-held.
• You write clearly. Not beautifully - just clearly and quickly.
• You have good judgment about what matters and what doesn’t.
Highly preferred:
• Some exposure to B2B GTM, sales ops, or startup environments
• Comfortable with tools like Clay, Notion, Make/Zapier, HubSpot, or equivalents - or fast enough to pick them up
• You follow the US startup ecosystem - you know who YC is, what pre-seed means, why founder-led sales works
• You’re the person in your friend group who’s already automated something everyone else still does manually
What This Is Not
• A structured program with defined learning goals. There’s no curriculum.
• A comfortable 9-to-5. The work is real and the pace is real.
• A stepping stone you phone in. If you’re not genuinely excited about AI and startups, this will be obvious fast.
What You Get
• Direct access to a founder running two companies across AI product and services
• You’ll see the full picture - GTM, ops, client work, strategy - not a slice of it
• Fast career surface area. If you’re good, you’ll own things quickly.
• Competitive comp for the role level
Apply by telling us two things:what you’ve built with AI, and the last thing you figured out completely on your own.

This role offers broad exposure across HR and is a strong path toward HR Business Partnering.

About the role

The HR Generalist serves an important role for the organization as a link between ESC operations and HR Business Partners (HRBPs). You’ll take in, sort and resolve routine but nuanced HR work: manager coaching, performance management, annual review, and project support across multiple areas.


You will get to:

  • Serve as a frontline point of contact for managers, coaching them through nuanced HR questions with guidance based on policy, practice and risk.
  • Run detailed inquiries with employees and ask the right follow-up questions to gather the facts, timeline, and route it to the right team to support.
  • Partner with HRBPs to execute people and talent strategies, including performance, annual review, and position management efforts, ensuring operational details are managed end-to-end.
  • Participate in HRBP team meetings, talent forums, and relevant syncs to stay current on business context and bring insights back into ESC operations.
  • Coordinate with partners to ensure end-to-end case completeness and smooth employee and manager experience across teams.
This role has been categorized as a Remote position. “Remote” employees do not have a permanent corporate office workplace and, instead, work from a physical location of their choice, which must be identified to the Company. U.S. employees may live in any of the 50 United States, with limited exceptions.In California, Connecticut, Maryland, Massachusetts, New Jersey, New York, Washington state, and Washington DC the standard base pay range for this role is $86,200.00 - $137,800.00 annually. This base pay range is specific to these locations and may not be applicable to other locations.In Colorado, Hawaii, Illinois, Maine, Minnesota, Nevada, Ohio, Rhode Island, Vermont, and Virginia the standard base pay range for this role is $81,900.00 - $130,900.00 annually. The base pay range is specific to these locations and may not be applicable to other locations.In addition to a competitive base salary this position is also eligible for equity awards based on factors such as experience, performance and location. Actual amounts will vary depending on experience, performance and location. Employees in this role will not be paid below the salary threshold for exempt employees in the state where they reside.

Who you are

  • Comfortable in the gray space - you enjoy working through situations with multiple stakeholders and turning ambiguous requests into clear next steps.
  • Energized by coaching managers in a way that balances employee experience, fairness and risk.
  • Organized and focused on execution. You juggle many requests and close the loop with clean documentation.
  • Systems, data, and AI-savvy. You’re excited to use AI tools to work faster, spot patterns and find better ways to support managers and employees.
  • A trusted collaborator across teammates who is comfortable working both through tickets and through real-time collaboration (instant messages and live calls).
  • Enjoy creating or iterating on SOPs, playbooks, and triage rules based on case pattern analysis and partner feedback.
  • Highly discrete and reliable when working with sensitive or confidential information related to performance, employee relations, or organizational changes.

Qualifications

  • 2+ years HR experience in shared services, employee service centers, employee relations, HR operations, or HR generalist roles
  • Experience conducting employee or manager inquires and documenting them clearly and objectively
  • Sound judgment in triaging, routing and escalating work based on complexity, risk and business context
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to create clear guidance
  • Proficiency with Workday (or similar HRIS) and ServiceNow (or similar tools)

Preferred Qualifications

  • Prior experience in an HR shared services / tiered support model or similar model where routing, SLAs, and escalation accuracy are core to success.
  • Hands-on experience using AI tools (such as ChatGPT, Claude or Gemini) to improve workflows, documentation or analysis
  • Experience supporting organizational change, re-leveling, or job profile work as a project contributor (project management, documentation, stakeholder prep) alongside HRBPs and COEs

Get to know us

At Zillow, we’re reimagining how people move—through the real estate market and through their careers. As the most-visited real estate platform in the U.S., we help people navigate buying, selling, financing and renting with greater ease and confidence. Whether you're working in tech, sales, operations, or design, you’ll be part of a company reshaping an industry and helping more people make home a reality.


How we work is a key part of that transformation. Through Cloud HQ, our strategic approach to distributed work, most employees have the flexibility to work from wherever they’re most productive—enabling us to move fast, stay connected and deliver on our people promise.


Zillow is honored to be recognized among the best workplaces in the U.S. Zillow was named one of FORTUNE 100 Best Companies to Work For® in 2026, and included on TIME’s America’s Best Companies 2026 list, reflecting our commitment to creating an innovative, inclusive, and engaging culture where employees are empowered to grow.


No matter where you sit in the organization, your work will help drive innovation, support our customers, and move the industry—and your career—forward, together.


Zillow Group is an equal opportunity employer committed to fostering an inclusive, innovative environment with the best employees. We are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, citizenship, marital status, disability, gender identity or Veteran status. If you have a disability or special need that requires accommodation, please contact your recruiter directly.


Qualified applicants with arrest or conviction records will be considered for employment in accordance with applicable state and local law.


Los Angeles County applicants: Job duties for this position include: work safely and cooperatively with other employees, supervisors, and staff; adhere to standards of excellence despite stressful conditions; communicate effectively and respectfully with employees, supervisors, and staff to ensure exceptional customer service; and follow all federal, state, and local laws and Company policies. Criminal history may have a direct, adverse, and negative relationship with some of the material job duties of this position. These include the duties and responsibilities listed above, as well as the abilities to adhere to company policies, exercise sound judgment, effectively manage stress and work safely and respectfully with others, exhibit trustworthiness and professionalism, and safeguard business operations and the Company’s reputation. Pursuant to the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records.

About the role

DRB builds the software that runs the modern car wash: point of sale, membership and recurring billing, payments, tunnel controls, and the analytics behind them. Our Solution Consulting team sits between customers, Sales, Product, and Customer Success, and exists to answer one question for every operator we work with: how do we help you grow, and what does the evidence say?

As a Solution Consultant you will do exactly that. You will dig into a customer's transaction, membership, and payment data to find what is actually happening in their business; frame the findings as clear recommendations an executive can act on; and build the demos, analyses, business cases, and prototypes that move enterprise deals and strategic accounts forward. You will use AI tools every day, not as a novelty but as the way we get quality work out faster than anyone expects.

This is a generalist seat on a small, flat team. You will not own a single lane. In a given month you may present a payment health review to a multi-site operator's leadership, build a pricing model for an RFP response, stand up a working AI prototype for a trade show, and write the talk track a sales rep uses to handle a competitive objection. If that range sounds energizing rather than exhausting, keep reading.

What you'll do

Solution analysis and enterprise sales support
• Partner with Enterprise Sales on RFP responses, solution designs, hosting and pricing cost models, growth-incentive structures, and executive pitch narratives.
• Perform gap analyses to assess solution readiness for car wash operators moving to Patheon, DRB's latest platform — identifying functional, operational, and data gaps and defining what it takes to close them.
• Assess customer requirements against DRB's platform and be honest about fit, gaps, and workarounds; write the talk tracks that help reps navigate them.
• Build and maintain competitive intelligence and battlecards on the car wash technology landscape.
• Support Sales-to-Implementation handoffs and drive process improvements so what we sell is what gets delivered.

AI, prototyping, and innovation

  • Use AI tools (Claude and similar) as a daily working method to draft analyses, generate prototypes, structure research, and produce customer-ready deliverables at speed and quality.
    • Build working prototypes and demos: interactive HTML and Streamlit applications, AI-driven sales and service agents, kiosk and trade show experiences, and internal tools such as quoting integrations with Salesforce.
    • Contribute to DRB's internal AI enablement programs (prompt libraries, prototyping playbooks) that help colleagues across the business adopt the same methods.

Communication and enablement

  • Present to audiences from a single-site owner to a multi-site operator's executive team to Vontier leadership, adjusting depth and language for each without losing the substance.
    • Write clearly: executive summaries, customer-facing reports, Q&A documents, and internal briefs that people actually read and act on.
    • Represent DRB at trade shows and customer events, running demos and handling technical and commercial questions on the floor.
    Customer analytics and advisory
    • Lead data deep dives for enterprise and strategic accounts covering payments, membership, churn, and site performance, including benchmarking and post-migration health reviews.
    • Translate findings into prioritized recommendations, quantified business impact, and next steps, delivered in decks, written reports, and live discovery sessions with customer leadership.
    • Contribute to DRB's customer intelligence platform (Pulse) and the quarterly advisory cadence we run with top accounts, including new dashboards, report templates, and analytical methods.
    • Run joint discovery sessions with customers to surface the right questions, then coordinate internal owners across Product, Engineering, Legal, and Payments to get them answered.

Who you are

  • Four or more years in solution consulting, pre-sales engineering, customer analytics, management consulting, or a similar customer-facing analytical role, ideally in SaaS, payments, or retail/consumer subscription businesses.
    • Fluent with data: comfortable in SQL and a modern warehouse (we use Snowflake), able to build and defend an analysis end to end, and able to explain what the numbers mean to someone who will never look at the query.
    • A practitioner with AI tools. You already use them to do real work, you understand where they are reliable and where they are not, and you can show examples.
    • Structured thinker who can take an ambiguous customer or executive question, break it into what needs to be true, and get to a defensible answer with imperfect information.
    • Strong writer and presenter. You produce polished documents, decks, and prototypes without a designer, and you can hold a room.
    • Commercially minded: you understand how pricing, contracts, and incentives shape a deal, and you keep the customer's growth and DRB's margin in view at the same time.
    • Comfortable working across Sales, Product, Engineering, Legal, and Customer Success, driving things to closure without formal authority.

Nice to have

  • Experience in car wash, fuel and convenience, QSR, or another multi-site operator segment.
    • Familiarity with card payments and recurring billing.
    • Hands-on with Python, Streamlit, HTML/JavaScript, or Salesforce for building prototypes and internal tools.
    • Exposure to RFP and enterprise procurement processes, or to M&A and market evaluation work.

How we work

The Solution Consulting team is five people across data, technical, innovation, and marketing consulting disciplines, and everyone is expected to reach across those lines. We favor shipping a useful artifact this week over a perfect one next quarter, we use AI aggressively and hold the output to a professional standard, and we measure ourselves by whether customers grow and deals close. You will have direct exposure to DRB and Vontier leadership and a wide license to propose what we should build next.

The base compensation range for this position is $95,000.00 to $115,000.00 per annum. Your actual base salary will be determined based upon numerous factors which may include relevant experience, skills, location (labor market data), credentials (education, certifications), and internal equity.

For this specific role, you may be eligible to participate in an annual bonus plan.

Vontier partners with you and your family on your health and wellness journey. Visit VontierBenefits.com to view our benefits. We offer a premium suite of health and wellness programs for you and your family, including medical, dental, vision, disability and life insurance. With programs for family planning from Maven Clinic to managing diabetes like Livongo, coverage for women's health, support for adult and elder care, paid parental leave, a generous 401(k) plan with matching company contributions, and more. Vontier is here for all stages of life. We also offer paid time off up to 120 hours each year, 14 paid holidays and paid sick leave.*

Disclaimer: The salary, other compensation, and benefits information is accurate as of the date of this posting. Sick leave amount may vary based on state or local laws applicable to the applicant’s geographic location.       <title>ZoomInfo Technologies LLC: Director, Applied AI</title>
      <region>Anywhere in the World</region>
      <category>Full-Stack Programming</category>
      <description>

<p>
  <strong>Headquarters:</strong> Bethesda, Maryland, United States; Remote-US-MA; Remote-US-MD; Remote-US-WA; Vancouver, Washington, United States; Waltham, Massachusetts, United States
</p>

<div class="content-intro"><p>ZoomInfo is where careers accelerate. We move fast, think boldly, and empower you to do the best work of your life. You’ll be surrounded by teammates who care deeply, challenge each other, and celebrate wins. With tools that amplify your impact and a culture that backs your ambition, you won’t just contribute. You’ll make things happen–fast.</p></div><div>
<p class="markdown-p">You'll lead the team that builds the intelligence every ZoomInfo AI agent reasons over — what's true about companies and the people in them, how they relate, and what they're buying. This role owns the B2B data graph strategy end to end, blending classical machine learning and data science with LLM and agentic systems, and treating evaluation and inference cost as core disciplines. You'll set the technical bar for a team of senior engineers while staying close to the code, shipping alongside the people you lead.</p>
<p class="markdown-p"><strong class="markdown-strong">What You'll Do</strong></p>
<ul class="markdown-ul">
<li class="markdown-li">You will ship code alongside your team, prototype alone to prove or kill an idea, and review code as a peer, setting how the team uses agentic coding tools with precise specifications and rigorous review.</li>
<li class="markdown-li">You will own delivery end-to-end, from problem framing through serving and on-call, including long-tail graph coverage and user memory for agents that separates user-supplied context from system-of-record data.</li>
<li class="markdown-li">You will choose the right method for each problem — classical machine learning, language models, or code — for challenges like sparse-company revenue estimation, entity resolution, and semantic intent modeling, deciding on measured evidence and stopping work that won't pay off.</li>
<li class="markdown-li">You will define what it takes to claim an agent's output is correct, not just that its run completed, building the evaluation datasets, regression gates, and experiment designs that back those claims.</li>
<li class="markdown-li">You will own inference cost, latency, and capacity, including build-versus-buy and distillation decisions, since a model too expensive to run everywhere isn't a result.</li>
<li class="markdown-li">You will hire and grow machine learning engineers, data scientists, and research engineers, developing senior engineers into technical leaders.</li>
<li class="markdown-li">You will work across product, platform, security, and legal, and present results and their limits to executives, including when a system isn't good enough to launch.</li>
</ul>
<p class="markdown-p"><strong class="markdown-strong">What You Bring</strong></p>
<p class="markdown-p"><em class="markdown-em">Must-Have:</em></p>
<ul class="markdown-ul">
<li class="markdown-li">You have significant experience building production machine learning systems and leading the engineers who build them by shipping alongside them — demonstrated capability matters more than years.</li>
<li class="markdown-li">You have a track record of hiring and developing senior machine learning engineers and data scientists against a high bar.</li>
<li class="markdown-li">You stay hands-on today: shipping code, building prototypes independently, and using agentic coding tools daily with rigorous review.</li>
<li class="markdown-li">You bring deep classical machine learning and data science expertise (supervised learning, feature engineering, statistical inference and experiment design, strong SQL) alongside production LLM and agentic systems, with the judgment to choose between them, including setting an evaluation bar with leakage-safe validation, calibration, and validated LLM judges.</li>
<li class="markdown-li">You have a record of cost and capacity decisions for model serving, such as moving a workload from a hosted model to a distilled or self-hosted one, with the savings measured, and you report results to executives with their limits stated, including recommending against a launch.</li>
</ul>
<p class="markdown-p"><em class="markdown-em">Preferred:</em></p>
<ul class="markdown-ul">
<li class="markdown-li">You bring entrepreneurial experience — founding a company, or taking a product from inception to paying customers as a founding or early engineer.</li>
<li class="markdown-li">You have experience in propensity modeling, ranking and retrieval, clustering, or entity resolution at scale.</li>
<li class="markdown-li">You have worked on web-scale language processing over multilingual, noisy text, knowledge graphs, or user memory for agents.</li>
<li class="markdown-li">You have experience with post-training and distillation, open-weight model serving, or AI governance and safety practices (ISO/IEC 42001, NIST AI RMF).</li>
</ul>
<p class="markdown-p">&nbsp;</p>
<p class="markdown-p">#LI-hybrid</p>
